snapshot.title: UPSC IR 2: Multilateral Orgs & Summits
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ UPSC v12.0 Hook: QUAD: Indo-Pacific. G20: One Earth. BRICS: Shanghai Bank. SCO: Security. AU: G20 New Member.

quick_notes.title: QUAD
quick_notes.detail: India, USA, Japan, Australia. "Free and Open Indo-Pacific". Not a military alliance (officially).
quick_notes.explanation: QUAD stands for the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue, which is a group of four countries: India, the United States of America (USA), Japan, and Australia. The group works together to promote a "Free and Open Indo-Pacific," meaning they want to keep the Indian and Pacific Ocean regions peaceful, stable, and accessible to all nations without any single country dominating them. Officially, the QUAD is not a military alliance, so it does not have a formal treaty that requires members to defend each other in case of an attack. Instead, it focuses on practical cooperation in areas like maritime security, disaster response, technology, and infrastructure.

quick_notes.title: G20 (India 2023)
quick_notes.detail: Theme: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam. Inclusion of African Union as permanent member. Global Biofuel Alliance.
quick_notes.explanation: The Group of Twenty, or G20, is a forum of the world's 19 largest economies plus the European Union, and it was created to discuss and coordinate global economic and financial policies. When India hosted the G20 in 2023, the main theme was "Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam," which is a Sanskrit phrase meaning "the world is one family," and this idea guided all the discussions about unity and shared global challenges. A major outcome of India's 2023 G20 presidency was the permanent inclusion of the African Union as a full member of the G20, which means the 55 countries of Africa now have a permanent seat and a stronger voice at the table of the world's biggest economies. Another key achievement was the launch of the Global Biofuel Alliance, which is a group of countries that agree to work together to increase the use of clean fuels made from plants and organic waste, like ethanol, so that nations can reduce their dependence on polluting fossil fuels.

quick_notes.title: BRICS
quick_notes.detail: Brazil, Russia, India, China, SA. Recent expansion (Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE joined). NDB (New Dev Bank) HQ: Shanghai.
quick_notes.explanation: BRICS is an international group of major emerging economies, originally formed by Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa (the "S" originally stood for South Africa, which joined in 2010). The group was created to promote economic cooperation and give these countries a stronger voice in global affairs, especially as an alternative to Western-dominated institutions like the World Bank and IMF (International Monetary Fund). In 2024, BRICS expanded its membership to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE), making it a larger and more diverse bloc. One of BRICS's key institutions is the New Development Bank (NDB), also called the BRICS Bank, which was established to fund infrastructure and sustainable development projects in member countries and other developing nations. The NDB's headquarters (HQ) is located in Shanghai, China, and it was officially opened in 2015. The bank provides loans and financial support without the strict conditions often attached by Western financial institutions, allowing member nations more flexibility in their development plans.

quick_notes.title: SCO (Shanghai Coop Org)
quick_notes.detail: India & Pakistan joined in 2017. Security-focused. RATS (Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure).
quick_notes.explanation: SCO (Shanghai Cooperation Organisation) is a group of countries that work together on security, like fighting terrorism, and on economic and political issues. India and Pakistan both became full members of this group in 2017. RATS stands for Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure, which is a part of the SCO that helps member countries share information and plan joint actions to stop terrorist activities.

quick_notes.title: UNSC Reforms
quick_notes.detail: India seeking permanent seat. G4 (India, Brazil, Japan, Germany) supports each other.
quick_notes.explanation: The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) is the main body responsible for keeping international peace. Currently, it has five permanent members with veto power, like the USA and China. India wants to become a permanent member, meaning it would have a permanent seat and the power to block decisions. To push for this change, India joined a group called the G4, which includes Brazil, Japan, and Germany. All four of these countries support each other's bids for permanent seats in the Security Council. The G4 demands UNSC reforms to expand the number of permanent members beyond the original five.
